thread:
alex_support: :wave: Customer hitting 400 on tool/function call when building JSON payload in PowerShell. They say it works on mac/linux but fails on Windows. Repro + logs below.

maria_customer: Posting exact commands they used so you can repro.
```
# PowerShell on Windows 10/11
$payload = '{"query":"find cats"}'
$meta = '{"user":"maria"}'
# naive concat to combine JSON pieces
$body = $payload + "," + $meta
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d $body
```

maria_customer: Response from API: 
```
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{"error":"tool_args: invalid json: unexpected trailing comma at position 27"}
```

alex_support: Notes: customer says they tried escaping quotes and switching single/double quotes; still get invalid JSON. They can repro locally on Windows Server Core image. @sam_engineer can you take a look? :thinking_face:

sam_engineer: Looking. On PS the concatenation here produces a string like `{"query":"find cats"},{"user":"maria"}` which is not valid top-level JSON (two objects separated by comma). Also PowerShell may add extra double-quoting depending on how curl receives the arg. Two quick suggestions: compose a single object or use an array; better: build a PowerShell object and ConvertTo-Json to get a single serialized JSON string.

sam_engineer: Example quick fix to repro and to send properly:
```
# build as object and serialize
$bodyObj = @{ query = 'find cats'; user = 'maria' }
$body = $bodyObj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 1 -Compress
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/run -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d $body
```

zoe_devex: This smells like a doc/faq gap — we should add a note about PowerShell string concat pitfalls and recommend ConvertTo-Json or writing to a temp file and using `--data-binary @file.json`. Also mention `--data-raw` subtlety.

infra-bot: Reproduced on windows-ltsc-2022 image in our test matrix. Attach logs: `curl` received body length 54, content started with `{\"query\":...},{\"user\":...}` which our parser interprets as two top-level values (invalid).

maria_customer: I tried `--data-raw` and writing to file as suggested, confirmed it works. Example that fixed it for me:
```
$body = @{ query = 'find cats'; user = 'maria' } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
Set-Content -Path .\body.json -Value $body -Encoding utf8
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/run -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @body.json
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"result":"ok","task_id":"t_12345"}
```

alex_support: Great, customer confirmed. Root cause summary: malformed tool args caused by naive string concatenation in PowerShell producing multiple JSON fragments (and double-escaping when passed to curl). Action items: (1) add PowerShell doc note and `ConvertTo-Json` example (zoe), (2) add automated test case on windows-ltsc for naive concat pattern (sam), (3) update support KB with troubleshooting steps (alex).

alex_support: Closing thread after customer confirmation. Thanks everyone :+1:
